scope: Half Brake–Reuss lap-jointed beam. Predict conditional phase and force-curve SHAPE on every released response-controlled sweep; absolute input-force gain is not supplied by the release.
training: Only the separate shaker ringdown DIC/acceleration and matched author PFF decay summaries. Hammer is unusable as a force calibration without the time waveform. Unknown input gain is retained. No forced arrays used to develop, choose or scale any model.
test: All eight RC curves in released acquisition order, all original frequency steps; FC four curves completely excluded from scientific access. RC frequency and realized collocated acceleration-amplitude are the only test explanatory fields; response phase and force are held outcomes. This is a conditional inverse task. No evaluation of prospective command tracking or forward FC amplitude.

contrast.candidate: Spatial energy-loss model. Infer displacement amplitude X, frequency ω and amplitude-dependent effective mode mass from the published bottom-side DIC field normalized at the acceleration-3 location, and damping or decay of its spatial velocity energy. Under near-single-mode balance form the reactive/dissipative components of driving-point force. Common unknown mass/gain is irrelevant to the registered shape. These are model assumptions; finite linewidth, other modes, damping and a changing mode shape can invalidate them.
contrast.primary_comparator: Measured-source author PFF frequency and damping versus displacement amplitude at the same acceleration location, using constant mode mass and real collocated force projection. Exact site correspondence or a documented deterministic amplitude-ratio map from training is required. Document separately that full MATLAB SSMLearn is fitted only to the same decay and is not a released forced-response predictor.
controls: Linear constant-frequency/damping version estimated from the same decay
Same measured decay law and energy formula with constant spatial mode shape, isolating the changing-mass term
Source acceleration-only backbone estimate as a separate control.

physics: Use exp(+iΩt). X=measured acceleration amplitude/Ω². Recorded force-to-acceleration phase arg(a/F)=π−arg([reactive]+i[dissipative]) under positive collocated projection. Added π comes from a=−Ω²x. Because source identifies relative phase but not sensor polarity/FFT sign, primary θ=atan2(|sin φ|,|cos φ|) in [0,π/2], sign/polarity invariant; θ=0 aligned or antialigned, θ=π/2 quadrature. Signed phases, if reported, descriptive only. A force-magnitude curve is normalized by that predictor’s OWN RMS over every row of that acquisition curve: no measured force used in prediction. Scoring separately maps each observed curve to its unit-RMS shape. No constant fit or minimization against held targets.
gates: For each curve compute angular MAE in degrees between folded observed/predicted phases, and RMSE of separately normalized nonnegative force shape. Equal-weight macro average of the eight curves for both metrics; primary joint requires strictly lower macro phase MAE AND shape RMSE than the authentic PFF constant-mass arm, and no larger maximum per-curve shape RMSE. Also report every arm/curve, all acquisition directions, worst observed row in each metric, full dimensioned force unknown. No significance claim for eight curves on one apparatus; no selection of “stable” branches, omit no row. Zero-RMS or nonfinite/incompatible data invalidate the specified gate, not grounds to drop a sweep.
boundaries: Models may be constructed on training files only, with the final algorithms/parameters/coefficients frozen before any conditional target input is admitted. Preserve intermediate failures and endpoint coverage. Interpolation beyond fitted acceleration/displacement support uses nearest trained endpoint (record number/range of clamped rows per curve; no test-based tuning). If same-site PFF/calibration or independently checkable physically interpretable model cannot be resolved, stop before protected outcomes. Do not claim absolute force from unknown input gain.
